questions.question: Why isn't BFS from an arbitrary vertex a topological sort?

options.a: A dependency may be discovered after the task that needs it

questions.section: Topological sorting is not BFS on arbitrary vertices
questions.explain: Kahn's algorithm only releases a node when all its prerequisites are done.

questions.question: How does Kahn's algorithm detect a cycle?

options.a: It outputs fewer than V vertices

questions.explain: Nodes on a cycle never reach in-degree 0.

questions.question: Why does BFS give shortest paths in unweighted graphs?

options.a: Nodes are discovered in nondecreasing distance order

questions.section: Why BFS yields shortest paths for unit weights
questions.explain: The first discovery of a node is along a shortest path.

questions.question: How do you make a topological order deterministic?

options.a: Shuffle neighbours
options.b: Pick ready nodes with a heap / sorted order

questions.explain: Ties between ready nodes are then broken the same way every run.

questions.question: Why does Dijkstra require non-negative edge weights?

options.a: A settled vertex could later get a shorter path through a negative edge

questions.section: Deep dive: two greedy proofs that use different structures
questions.explain: The greedy 'closest first' proof relies on paths never getting shorter.

questions.question: What is a stale heap entry in Dijkstra?

options.a: An entry whose distance is larger than the best now known for that vertex

questions.explain: Skip it on pop instead of decreasing keys.

questions.question: Union–find answers which question quickly?

options.a: Shortest path
options.b: Are a and b in the same component?

questions.explain: With path compression and union by rank, in near-constant amortised time.

questions.question: Kruskal on a disconnected graph produces…

options.a: a spanning tree
options.b: a minimum spanning forest with fewer than V − 1 edges

questions.explain: Count the edges to detect it.

questions.question: What four things define a dynamic program?

options.a: State, transition, base case, iteration order

questions.explain: Without a precise state, the recurrence can't be checked.

questions.question: In LCS, what does dp[i][j] mean?

options.a: LCS length of a[:i] and b[:j]

questions.explain: Prefix states make the recurrence well-defined.

questions.question: Iterating amounts in increasing order with coins in the inner loop allows…

options.a: each coin at most once

questions.section: Deep dive: iteration order encodes resource reuse
questions.explain: best[a − c] may already include coin c.

questions.question: Why can LIS 'tails' be kept with binary search?

options.a: tails[k] is the smallest possible tail of an increasing subsequence of length k+1, and tails is sorted

questions.explain: A smaller tail dominates a larger one of the same length.

questions.question: What must happen after exploring from a marked grid cell?

options.a: Restore the cell so other paths can use it

questions.section: State restoration is the core invariant
questions.explain: Marking prevents reuse within one path only.

questions.question: How does a trie speed up multi-word grid search?

options.a: It stops paths whose prefix matches no word

questions.explain: Pruning on prefixes cuts most of the search tree.

questions.question: In the two-sorted-arrays median, binary search runs over…

options.a: the values
options.b: the cut position in the shorter array

questions.explain: The other cut position follows from the total size.

questions.question: Why is honest complexity accounting important for backtracking?

options.a: Its worst case is exponential and depends on branching and output size

questions.section: Deep dive: exhaustive search requires honest complexity accounting
questions.explain: State branching factor, depth and output size.

questions.question: Which algorithm fits non-negative weighted edges best?

options.a: BFS

questions.section: 1. Start with a model, not a familiar implementation
questions.explain: BFS ignores weights; Bellman–Ford works but is slower: O(VE).

questions.question: Why does Dijkstra fail with a negative edge?

options.a: A vertex settled early can later be reached more cheaply

questions.explain: The proof assumes extending a path never makes it cheaper.

questions.question: How many rounds does Bellman–Ford need without negative cycles?
questions.explain: A shortest path has at most V − 1 edges.

questions.question: Bellman–Ford detects a negative cycle when…

options.a: a distance still improves in round V

questions.explain: Without a negative cycle, distances are final after V − 1 rounds.

questions.question: In DFS cycle detection, an edge to which kind of node proves a cycle?

options.a: An unvisited node
options.b: A node still on the current DFS path (grey)

questions.explain: Edges to finished nodes are cross or forward edges, not cycles.

questions.question: A topological order exists exactly when…

options.a: the graph is connected
options.b: the directed graph has no cycle

questions.explain: Any cycle makes 'before' impossible to satisfy.

questions.question: What does collapsing each SCC into one node produce?

options.a: A DAG

questions.explain: All cycles live inside components.

questions.question: How should parallel edges affect Kahn's in-degrees?

options.a: Count each edge consistently (or de-duplicate first)

questions.explain: Mismatched counting leaves nodes stuck with positive in-degree.

questions.question: Which question comes first when designing a DP?

options.a: What exactly does one state value mean?

questions.section: 1. The four questions every DP needs
questions.explain: Transitions and order follow from a precise state.

questions.question: Interval DP is filled in order of…

options.a: increasing interval length

questions.explain: Each interval depends on strictly shorter ones.

questions.question: Top-down memoised recursion vs bottom-up tables…

options.a: compute the same states; top-down may hit the recursion limit

questions.explain: Choose for clarity and depth constraints.

questions.question: A grid DP that ignores walls will…

options.a: count paths through blocked cells

questions.explain: Blocked cells must contribute 0 paths.

questions.question: Why does 0/1 knapsack iterate capacity downwards in a 1-D array?

options.a: So best[c − w] still refers to the previous item row

questions.explain: Upwards would reuse the current item.

questions.question: What does tails[k] store in the O(n log n) LIS?

options.a: The smallest possible last value of an increasing subsequence of length k+1

questions.explain: A smaller tail is always at least as useful.

questions.question: When can a 2-D DP table be compressed to one row?

options.a: When each row depends only on the previous row (in a safe order)

questions.explain: Check which cells are read before they are overwritten.

questions.question: An optimisation of a DP is valid when…

options.a: it runs faster on examples
options.b: you can prove it computes the same recurrence

questions.explain: Speed without a proof is a guess.

questions.question: Why can't a Fenwick tree answer range-minimum queries directly?

options.a: Minimum has no inverse, so prefix(hi) − prefix(lo) doesn't apply

questions.explain: Segment trees only need an associative combine with an identity.

questions.question: What does `i & -i` compute?

options.a: The lowest set bit of i

questions.explain: It is the size of the range node i is responsible for.

questions.question: Data never changes and you need many range sums. Best choice?

options.a: Segment tree

questions.section: 4. When not to reach for advanced structures
questions.explain: O(1) per query after O(n) preprocessing.

questions.question: Update and query costs of Fenwick and segment trees?

options.a: O(1) and O(n)

questions.explain: Both walk a logarithmic-height structure.

questions.question: Amortised O(1) append means…

options.a: every append is O(1)
options.b: a sequence of n appends costs O(n) in total

questions.explain: Occasional O(n) resizes are paid for by many cheap appends.

questions.question: Path compression and union by size together make DSU operations…

options.a: O(n)

questions.explain: The bound grows so slowly it's effectively constant.

questions.question: The cut property says…

options.a: the lightest edge crossing any cut belongs to some MST
options.b: every edge belongs to an MST

questions.section: 3. MST correctness via the cut property
questions.explain: Kruskal adds exactly such edges.

questions.question: Why can't a rollback DSU use path compression?

options.a: Compression rewrites many parents, which a simple undo stack can't restore

questions.section: 4. Why rollback DSU needs special treatment
questions.explain: Union by size alone keeps trees O(log n) tall.

questions.question: Which three claims should you separate about an algorithm?

options.a: Termination, correctness, complexity

questions.explain: Each needs its own argument or evidence.

questions.question: A loop invariant must…

options.a: hold initially, be preserved by each iteration, and imply the result on exit

questions.section: 2. Loop invariant example: lower bound search
questions.explain: That is induction over iterations.

questions.question: Differential testing requires…

options.a: an independent oracle implementation

questions.explain: Disagreements reveal bugs in either implementation.

questions.question: What does a metamorphic test check?

options.a: A known output
options.b: A relation between outputs on related inputs (e.g. shuffled input, same result)

questions.explain: Useful when there's no oracle for the exact answer.

questions.question: What should you write before any code for a system-style algorithm problem?

options.a: The contract: inputs, outputs, ties, failure modes

questions.explain: Every later decision follows from it.

questions.question: Which data structure keeps the scheduler deterministic when several tasks are ready?

options.a: A heap with a total ordering key

questions.explain: Sets and dicts don't define an order you can rely on for ties.

questions.question: Adding task priorities to the scheduler changes…

options.a: only the heap key
options.b: the invariants and tie rules, which must be restated

questions.explain: State the new ordering rule and re-check correctness.

questions.question: A good interview presentation order is…

options.a: code, then contract

questions.explain: It shows reasoning, not just a result.
